Medicine walkthrough
This student chooses family medicine after comparing several clinical roles. The student prefers a physician’s diagnostic work and medical-school/residency preparation. Related nursing and PA routes stay available to compare.
Fictional development case. Includes shared scripted defaults.

LIFESTYLE 1. Where would you feel at home?
Answer: My own space — A comfortable one-bedroom apartment.
Choices: Share a place — A room of your own. Shared living space. | A small place — A modest apartment with the basics. | [selected] My own space — A comfortable one-bedroom apartment. | Room to spread out — A larger apartment or rental home. | A standout home — A high-end home with extra space and comforts.

Include upkeep and a replacement fund. | [selected] A reliable used car — A compact car for everyday trips. | A newer car — More comfort and newer features. | A premium car — A car that is part of the experience.

LIFESTYLE 9. How much room would you like for future goals?

FOLLOW-UP 9. Which responsibility would you most want to learn about?

FOLLOW-UP 10. Which professional would you like to follow for a day?

Answer: College, medical school, then a medical residency.

How to get there
Medical school, residency, and a Texas physician license.
Complete college prerequisites and an MD or DO.
Family medicine residency usually takes 3 years.
Meet Texas licensing exams, training, and eligibility requirements.
College About 4 years
MD or DO About 4 years
Paid residency Usually 3 years in family medicine
About 11 years after high school for this common family medicine route. Other specialties differ.
College and medical school are required
College courses prepare you for medical school. A medical degree, residency, and a Texas license are required to work as a doctor.
